the call setup time can be reduced by using a more efficient compression scheme for SIP messages, by using TCP instead of UDP for SIP message transport, and by using a larger number of simultaneous SIP messages in transmission, while still keeping a high probability of success for call setup.

(1) SIP compression efficiency is the most important factor in reducing call setup time; and (2) the use of TCP as a signaling transport protocol is not a viable solution to reduce call setup time, as it introduces a significant delay in the signaling flow.

the signaling efficiency is improved by: (a) using TCP as transport protocol, (b) using a SIP message compression algorithm, and (c) using a signaling server that is located in the same network as the user.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the call setup time in all-IP networking is dominated by the time required for radio link establishment.

the signaling efficiency is a very important factor in the call setup time and it can be greatly improved by using the SIP over TCP protocol, the use of a single IMS server and the use of a compression mechanism for the SIP messages.
the call setup time is not a function of the radio link quality, but of the IMS architecture design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a detailed, bottom-up analysis of signaling efficiency for multimedia session establishment in all- IP wireless networks, based on a large set of design parameters across all network layers.
the call setup time can be reduced by 50-80%, depending on the system architecture and the choice of the signaling protocol.

the IMS signaling efficiency can be improved by 20% or more by using a combination of the following methods: a) using a SIP compressor that is aware of the IMS signaling flow; b) using UDP for the IMS signaling transport instead of TCP, and c) using an optimized radio link with a high packet error rate (PER) tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful system level design of the signaling protocol and the transport protocol is necessary to achieve the desired signaling efficiency.
, for interactive applications, the signaling overhead can be a significant factor in call setup delay.
the call setup time can be significantly reduced by using SIP compression and TCP for SIP signaling, which are not currently supported by the IMS framework.
